- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.18) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to avoid underreaction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment remains neutral/weak.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.30) and price is trending up, model often lags; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (0.18–0.36), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; smooth forecast toward recent 5-day average if sentiment is weak, or slightly accelerate if sentiment is strong.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period volatility (last 7–10 days); apply 1–2% upward adjustment if sentiment is positive or if recent price action shows acceleration.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.10) and price is falling, model often fails to anticipate further decline; add 0.5–1% downward buffer to avoid “too optimistic” recovery forecasts.
